adversarial_critique:
1. Numeric accuracy vs. substantive mischaracterization: Every printed statistic in Claude's stored row matches Table 5 (p. 8) and Section 3.1 (p. 6) verbatim (Local vs. No Management aOR = 3.733, Wald 95% CI 2.993–4.657, p < 0.0001; N = 11,065 Afridev hand pumps [9,089 functional, 1,976 non-functional]; Institutional aOR = 2.893 [2.349–3.562]; WASH Committee aOR = 2.426 [1.946–3.026]). However, two non-numeric extraction errors distort the row's substantive meaning: (a) Claude defines the exposure as water points maintained by 'a local authority' (following loose prose on pp. 6–7 and 10), whereas Table 1's variable definition note (p. 3) explicitly states that 'Local includes NGO, community, local group, and private owner'—making 'Local' a heterogeneous non-state/private/community catch-all rather than local government authority (and making 'Institutional vs. No Management' [schools, health facilities, other] or 'WASH Committee vs. No Management' cleaner governance contrasts); and (b) Claude claims the multivariable logistic regression controls for 'county', whereas County is only a node in the Bayesian Network (Figure 3, p. 10; Table 6, p. 12) and is not included in the multivariable logistic regression model (Table 1, p. 3; Table 5, p. 8). In addition, Table 5 adjusts for 'Damage Status' (explicitly labeled a 'Mediator' in Table 1) and 'Time it took to repair', inducing post-treatment mediator over-adjustment (attenuating the Local OR from 4.730 unadjusted to 3.733 adjusted), and relies on single hot-deck imputation for up to 30% missingness (2,539 entries in payment status) without multiple-imputation variance correction. The source paper itself also exhibits multiple text-vs-table errors (e.g., p. 7 cites unadjusted OR/CIs while discussing Table 5; p. 9 asserts no payment method was significant while citing p = 0.011 for post-breakdown payment; Table 5 mislabels 'Always Water vs. Seasonal' as 'Seasonal vs. Year-Around').

2. Questionable SWiM non-fit classification: Conditional on the study remaining included, leaving `synthesis_family` blank is questionable and inconsistent with Family C as broadly retitled under A21 (ownership, regulation, institutional capacity, and administrative/management structure). Claude's `provenance_note` explicitly reveals a taxonomic slip: it rejected Family C by misdefining Family C as 'a barrier restricting access (Family C)' rather than institutional/regulatory/management capacity, while acknowledging the exposure IS 'institutional management CAPACITY/responsibility-assignment'. Furthermore, `exclusion_from_pooling_reason` conflates quantitative meta-analytic pooling (`included_in_pooled_estimate = FALSE` because only one study uses this exact Liberian hand-pump operationalization) with SWiM narrative/vote-counting family membership (`synthesis_family`), which is designed specifically to synthesize direction of effect across non-identical institutional exposures.

3. Borderline review eligibility for PI scope check: Under the strict 2026-10-13/14 CK narrow Criterion 2 standard, S388 sits on the O&M engineering vs. administrative governance boundary and should be flagged as borderline for PI review. Its extracted predictor ('Who is maintaining the water point (routine repairs)?') evaluates operational O&M repair responsibility alongside hardware damage, mechanic toolkits, repair turnaround time, and spare-parts travel time—not a formal statute, legal mandate, tenure rule, or administrative eligibility rule—and its unit of analysis is the physical Afridev pump rather than the household, coding 'Yes—Functional (but not in use)' as functional.

number_verification_detail: All numeric values in `effect_sizes.csv` match the source PDF exactly: primary adjusted OR = 3.733 and Wald 95% CI = 2.993–4.657 (p < 0.0001; unadjusted OR = 4.730, 95% CI 3.950–5.665) for `Local vs No Management` in Table 5 (p. 8); `standard_error` is appropriately blank because Table 5 reports Wald 95% CIs without SEs; analytic sample size N = 11,065 Afridev hand pumps matches the Abstract (p. 1), Section 3.1 (p. 6, printed as `11, 065`), Section 4 (p. 12), and Table 4's sum (9,089 functional + 1,976 non-functional = 11,065, p. 7); and the secondary adjusted estimates cited in `provenance_note` match Table 5 verbatim (`Institutional vs No Management` aOR = 2.893, 95% CI 2.349–3.562; `WASH Committee vs No Management` aOR = 2.426, 95% CI 1.946–3.026). Two non-numeric discrepancies exist in the row metadata: (1) `adjusted` lists `county` as a multivariable logistic regression covariate, but `County` is absent from Table 1 (p. 3) and Table 5 (p. 8) and enters only the Bayesian Network model (Figure 3, p. 10; Table 6, p. 12); and (2) `exposure_definition` describes `Local` as `maintained by a local authority`, whereas Table 1's note (p. 3) defines `Local` as `NGO, community, local group, and private owner`.
